title: Versal rings after a finite residue-field extension
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means having a unique maximal ideal. Let $k$ be a finite extension of $R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-weil-field]. Schemes and algebraic spaces are [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. An algebraic stack is a category fibred in groupoids with effective etale descent for objects and sheaf descent for isomorphisms, diagonal representable by algebraic spaces, and a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Representable means that every scheme-valued 2-base change is an algebraic space. Smoothness is tested on smooth scheme atlases by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Locally of finite type means that a smooth scheme atlas has locally finite type composite to the base [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be an algebraic stack locally of finite type and let $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ be an $R$-point [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For an Artinian local $R$-algebra $A$ with specified residue field $k$, let $\mathcal F_x(A)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(\eta,\alpha)$ with $\eta\in\mathcal X(A)$ and $\alpha:\eta|_k\cong x$, with arrows respecting the marking. Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize; all maps between test algebras are local and induce the identity on their specified residue fields. Here a versal ring at $x$ means a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $C$ with residue field $k$, equipped with a marked formal object: objects $\eta_n\in\mathcal F_x(C/\mathfrak m_C^n)$, $n\geq1$, with coherent transition isomorphisms $\eta_{n+1}|_{C/\mathfrak m_C^n}\cong\eta_n$. For a test algebra $A$ and a local $R$-map $v:C\to A$ inducing the identity on $k$ (it kills some $\mathfrak m_C^n$), write $\eta_v\in\mathcal F_x(A)$ for the pullback of $\eta_n$ along the induced map $C/\mathfrak m_C^n\to A$. Versality means: for every surjection $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ of test algebras, every such $v:C\to A$, every $\zeta'\in\mathcal F_x(A')$ and every isomorphism $\zeta'|_A\cong\eta_v$ in $\mathcal F_x(A)$, there exist a local $R$-map $v':C\to A'$ lifting $v$ and an isomorphism $\zeta'\cong\eta_{v'}$ in $\mathcal F_x(A')$ restricting to the prescribed one. Let $C$ be a versal ring at $x$. Let $l/k$ be any specified finite field extension and let $x_l$ be the induced point. Then there exist a versal ring $C_l$ at $x_l$, complete Noetherian local with residue field $l$ and equipped with a marked formal object in the same sense, and a local $R$-map $C\to C_l$ inducing the specified embedding $k\hookrightarrow l$ and formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_{C_l}$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic].

source.place: Tag 0DQY, lemma-versal-ring-field-extension; proof invokes Formal Deformation Theory, Lemma 0DQF, lemma-change-of-field-versal-ring, and Artin's Axioms, Lemma 07WX, lemma-change-of-field.

proof.text: Choose finitely many $k$-algebra generators $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ of $l$: a finite $k$-basis is such a generating family, since every element is already a $k$-linear combination. Evaluation gives a surjection $e:P=C[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]\twoheadrightarrow l$, using $C\twoheadrightarrow k\hookrightarrow l$ on coefficients [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $\mathfrak q=\ker(e)$ and $D=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}P/\mathfrak q^n$. Apply [lem-sfb-artin-completed-polynomial-test-ring] with its base ring $C$, its residue field $l$, and its number $d$ of additional zero-valued variables equal to zero. It makes $D$ complete Noetherian local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qD$ and residue field canonically $l$, and makes every $B_n=D/\mathfrak m_D^n$ Artinian local with residue $l$. The structure map $j:C\to D$ induces the specified $k\hookrightarrow l$; its inverse image of $\mathfrak m_D$ is $\mathfrak m_C$, so it is local. Thus $D$ is a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 0DQF, lemma-change-of-field-versal-ring, construction of S; Tag 06SM, lemma-exists-smooth, polynomial-completion construction.

proof.text: The lifting clause of [lem-sfb-artin-completed-polynomial-test-ring], again with base $C$ and residue field $l$, says that every local residue-preserving $C$-map $D\to B$ lifts through every surjection $B'\twoheadrightarrow B$ of Artinian local $C$-algebras with residue field $l$. Apply [lem-sfb-adic-smooth-fixed-residue-lifting] with its base ring $C$, its finite residue extension $l/(C/\mathfrak m_C)=l/k$, and its complete local algebra $D$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1 and the hypotheses on $C$. This proves that $j:C\to D$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_D$-adic topology, in the precise unrestricted square-zero lifting sense required by the item.

source.place: Tag 0DQF, construction of S and formal smoothness; Tag 0DYL, lemma-smooth, equivalence (1) and (2).

proof.text: For any Artinian local $R$-algebra $B$ with residue map $B\twoheadrightarrow l$, put $A_B=B\times_l k$. By [lem-sfb-artinian-finite-residue-restriction], $A_B$ is Artinian local with residue $k$, its projection to $B$ is injective, and $B'\twoheadrightarrow B$ induces a surjection $A_{B'}\twoheadrightarrow A_B$. The construction respects the $R$-structures. Since $k$ and $l$ are finite over $R/\mathfrak m_R$, each is generated as an $R$-algebra by a finite vector-space basis. Hence [lem-sfb-artinian-finite-type-residue-criterion] makes $\operatorname{Spec}A_B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B$ finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}R$, as are $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\operatorname{Spec}l$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] makes $\ker(B\to l)=\mathfrak m_B$ nilpotent. These assertions verify all the Artinian, finite-type, and nilpotence hypotheses needed in the next step.

source.place: Tag 07W8, situation-change-of-fields, comparison functor and its properties; artin.tex Tag 07WX, finite-type pushout hypotheses.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-affine-closed-pinching-pushout] to $B\twoheadrightarrow l\leftarrow k$. It identifies $\operatorname{Spec}A_B$ with the scheme pushout $\operatorname{Spec}k\amalg_{\operatorname{Spec}l}\operatorname{Spec}B$. Here $\operatorname{Spec}l\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the nilpotent closed immersion just checked. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-rim-schlessinger] over the Noetherian base ring $R$ to obtain the restriction equivalence
$$\mathcal X(A_B)\simeq\mathcal X(k)\times_{\mathcal X(l)}\mathcal X(B).$$
The right side retains the specified isomorphism over $l$. All four schemes satisfy its finite-type hypothesis by step 3; the item supplies exactly its algebraic-stack hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 07WX, lemma-change-of-field, displayed pushout and restriction equivalence; Tag 07WQ, lemma-algebraic-stack-RS.

proof.text: Fixing the object $x$ and its marking in the equivalence of step 4 gives an equivalence $E_B:\mathcal F_x(A_B)\simeq\mathcal F_{x_l}(B)$: send $(w,\alpha)$ to its restriction to $B$, marked by $\alpha|_l$. Explicitly, a marked object $z$ over $B$ supplies the triple $(x,z,z|_l\cong x_l)$ and therefore lifts by essential surjectivity in step 4. An arrow between two images, compatible with their markings, pairs with the identity of $x$ to give an arrow of triples, and thus lifts uniquely by full faithfulness in step 4. This proves full faithfulness on marked groupoids as well. Restriction along $B\to B'$ commutes with $E$ up to the canonical pullback comparisons: both composites restrict the same object along $A_B\to B'$. These comparisons inherit their coherence from the given pullback functors.

source.place: Tag 07WX, lemma-change-of-field, restriction to marked fibre categories after the displayed equivalence.

proof.text: Let $(\eta_r)_{r\geq1}$ be the given marked formal object over $C$. For $B_n$ from step 1 put $A_n=A_{B_n}$. The composite $C\xrightarrow{j}D\to B_n$ has residue image in $k\subset l$, hence factors uniquely through the subring $A_n=B_n\times_l k$. The resulting map $u_n:C\to A_n$ is local and residue-preserving. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], $\mathfrak m_{A_n}^{r_n}=0$ for some $r_n$, so $u_n$ kills $\mathfrak m_C^{r_n}$. Pull back $\eta_{r_n}$ to $A_n$ and apply $E_{B_n}$ to obtain $\theta_n\in\mathcal F_{x_l}(B_n)$. For $B_{n+1}\to B_n$, the maps from $C$ to $A_n$ agree. Choose a common larger exponent for the two factorizations through quotients of $C$; the given transition isomorphisms of $\eta$ identify the two restrictions. They satisfy the cocycle identities because those of $\eta$ do, and the pullback comparisons in step 5 are coherent. Thus $(\theta_n)$ is a marked formal object over $D$. In particular, for any local residue-preserving $b:D\to B$, its pullback $\theta_b$ is canonically $E_B(\eta_{u_b})$, where $u_b:C\to A_B$ is the factorization of $bj$.

source.place: Tag 0DQF, lemma-change-of-field-versal-ring, transformation from the functor represented by S to the residue-changed functor represented by R.

proof.text:
We verify versality, retaining the prescribed isomorphism. Take $p:B'\twoheadrightarrow B$, a local residue-preserving $b:D\to B$, $\zeta'\in\mathcal F_{x_l}(B')$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:\zeta'|_B\xrightarrow{\sim}\theta_b$. By essential surjectivity of $E_{B'}$ choose $w'\in\mathcal F_x(A_{B'})$ and an isomorphism $\delta:E_{B'}(w')\xrightarrow{\sim}\zeta'$. By the naturality and full faithfulness in step 5, the composite $\gamma\circ\delta|_B$ has a unique preimage
$$\beta:w'|_{A_B}\xrightarrow{\sim}\eta_{u_b}.$$
Step 3 makes $A_{B'}\twoheadrightarrow A_B$ a surjection of the test algebras for $x$. Apply the assumed versality of $C$ to $u_b,w',\beta$. It supplies a local residue-preserving $u':C\to A_{B'}$ lifting $u_b$ and an isomorphism $\varepsilon:w'\xrightarrow{\sim}\eta_{u'}$ restricting to $\beta$.

source.place: Tag 0DQF, smoothness after change of field; artin.tex Tag 07WX, identification of the two marked deformation categories.

proof.text: Give $B'$ its $C$-algebra structure by $C\xrightarrow{u'}A_{B'}\to B'$ and give $B$ the compatible one $C\xrightarrow{u_b}A_B\to B$. Both have the specified $C$-algebra residue field $l$; the latter structure is $bj$, so $b:D\to B$ is a $C$-map for these structures. Apply the lifting clause of [lem-sfb-artin-completed-polynomial-test-ring] with base $C$ to lift $b$ to a local residue-preserving $C$-map $b':D\to B'$. Its composite with $j$ is the map just prescribed by $u'$, so the unique factorization $C\to A_{B'}$ associated to $b'$ is precisely $u'$. Consequently $E_{B'}(\varepsilon)\circ\delta^{-1}$ identifies $\zeta'$ with $\theta_{b'}$. Its restriction is $(\gamma\circ\delta|_B)\circ(\delta|_B)^{-1}=\gamma$, by the choice of $\beta$ and the restriction condition on $\varepsilon$. This is exactly the versality lifting property, including the prescribed isomorphism. Take $C_l=D$ with $(\theta_n)$ and $C\to C_l=j$. Step 1 gives its complete local Noetherian and residue-field clauses, and step 2 gives adic formal smoothness.
